transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Thanks for seeing me. I’m constantly worrying about everything—my kids, my job, money—and it feels like it never lets up. It's just getting to the point where I feel completely overwhelmed all the time.
Did these worries start after a specific stressful event or major life change, and have they been present most days for more than 6 months?

Yes, they started about a year ago when my contentious divorce was finalized and I took on a massive digital transformation project at work. It's been going on pretty much every single day since then, so it has definitely been over six months.
Along with the constant worry, do you also have periods of feeling very down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I wouldn't say I feel depressed, but I've definitely lost the ability to enjoy the things I used to love. Activities like community soccer, live music, or hiking are now completely overshadowed by my constant worrying, and I've even started bailing on plans with my friends because of it.
Besides losing interest, have you also been feeling down, hopeless, or depressed most days? Or is it mainly the constant worry and inability to relax?

It’s definitely the constant worry and the inability to relax rather than feeling depressed or hopeless. I just feel incredibly wound up and tense all the time, like there’s a motor running inside me that I can't turn off. My mind is always racing with "what-ifs" about everything and I just can't switch it off.
When you feel this worried and tense, do you also get physical symptoms like restlessness, muscle tension, fatigue, trouble concentrating, irritability, or sleep problems?

Yes, absolutely—I'm constantly clenching my jaw or jiggling my leg, and at night I just toss and turn for hours because my mind won't stop racing. I've also been incredibly irritable lately, snapping at my son and coworkers over the smallest things, which just leaves me feeling exhausted and guilty.
Do you ever have sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or feeling like you might die?

No, I don't really experience those sudden, overwhelming panic attacks or physical symptoms like chest pain or shortness of breath. Instead, my anxiety is more of a constant, low-grade tension and non-stop worrying that just stays with me throughout the day.

Do you ever have brief, sudden episodes of intense fear or panic that peak within minutes, with symptoms like a racing heart, shortness of breath, chest pain, or feeling like something terrible is about to happen?

No, I don't experience those sudden, brief spikes of intense panic or things like chest pain and shortness of breath. For me, it's just a constant, low-level tension and worry that stays with me the entire day.
How much has this constant worry and tension affected your daily life at work, at home, or in your relationships?

It’s had a massive impact across my whole life. At work, I've missed key project deadlines and my CIO actually pulled me aside because I seemed so distracted and tense. At home, I'm snapping at my kids and bailing on my friends, so I feel like my job and my relationships are really starting to slip.
Have you had any medical problems, started or changed any medications or substances, or increased caffeine/alcohol use around the time this anxiety began?

No, I haven't had any major medical issues or changes to my medications. My caffeine and alcohol use has stayed pretty much the same too, so nothing really changed on that front when the anxiety started.
Have you ever had a period of several days or more where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did impulsive things that were out of character?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that or felt unusually energized or euphoric. In fact, it's been the exact opposite—I feel constantly anxious, tense, and completely exhausted from tossing and turning all night.
Have you ever experienced a traumatic event, and do you have nightmares, flashbacks, or feel on edge because of it?

No, I haven't experienced any major traumatic events, and I don't have flashbacks or nightmares. While I definitely feel constantly on edge and tense, it’s driven by my ongoing worries about my work, kids, and finances rather than any past trauma.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has excessive, persistent worry about multiple areas (children, work, finances) for over 6 months, occurring nearly every day, with marked difficulty controlling the worry. He also has associated symptoms of restlessness/jitteriness, muscle tension, irritability, fatigue, sleep disturbance, and significant functional impairment at work and home. Panic disorder, PTSD, bipolar disorder, substance/medical causes, and major depression were not supported.
